title: I made a tiny adventure game for my daughter with Godot — I’d love your feedback
author: BambolandVr
selftext:
Hey everyone!

A little while ago I started making a small adventure game for my daughter, mostly as a fun personal project. I ended up turning it into a real little game using **Godot**, and now I’d love to hear what other people think about it.

It’s called **Adelaide: A Tiny Adventure**.  
🌐 Here’s the project page:  
[https://adelaideatinyadventure.studionamaste.net](https://adelaideatinyadventure.studionamaste.net/)

🎮 You can also play the current demo/femo for free on [itch.io](http://itch.io/):  
[https://theindiedad.itch.io/adelaide-a-tiny-adventure](https://theindiedad.itch.io/adelaide-a-tiny-adventure)

The game is very much a personal project, made with a lot of love (and a lot of learning along the way!). My daughter was the original reason I started it, but I’d now like to understand whether it works as a game for people who don’t know anything about it.

I’d really appreciate honest feedback, especially about:  
Did you understand what you were supposed to do?  
Did you enjoy exploring?  
What do you think of the art style and atmosphere?  
Was anything confusing or frustrating?  
Did the game make you curious about what happens next?

And if you’ve used **Godot** yourself, I’d also be really interested in hearing your thoughts from a development perspective.

Even a few minutes of play and a couple of comments would mean a lot to me.

Thanks for giving it a try! ❤️

comments.author: StayImpossible7013
comments.body:
Check your text in the menu. Examples: SE, BGM instead of "effects" and "music"  
Remove everything from menus that are not needed: Level selection when there's nothing to select, keyboard config, reset above, window scale (what is it even supposed to do?)  
Decide if game needs mouse or not. About me at least needs mouse to scroll and it doesn't even tell it scrollable with a scroll bar.  
Make multiple keys to default something. Running: A/D, left/right arrow, W or up arrow or space to jump.  
Exit game is not needed for web browser game as is.  
Double jump, weapon and jumping in the first place all were unintuitive. First thing I did was pressed space to jump and nothing happened. I did not assume that this cute girl would have weapon to kill monsters. Only after checking keyboard settings I realized that.  
Jumping to top of monster to kill them was also something I did not expect before trying it and realized you don't hurt yourself when jumping on the head of horned monster. (Spikes = death in typical game)  
I didn't know why to even try to collect coins. I just kept running and avoiding monsters.  
I don't see any progress. I gave up before reaching end of the first level. 500 seconds to finish first level seems like way too long. As a first time player I want to see some progress.  
The dog and cat that spoke to me felt like I should have achieved something at that point. Maybe they can "give" you double jump and the weapon as that I have at least some progress.  
The jumping monster does not show anything like it is preparing to jump. It just suddenly goes up and kills the player. Half a second different sprite would help player to avoid death.  
When changing running direction the background animation is wonky.  
Player can't see up enough to plan properly where to go.

Needs tutorial (story) to tell what can be done and why is she even running to right and killing monsters that are cute.

Good project and I assume it is something that people of any age can play for fun.

replies.author: BambolandVr
replies.body:
Thank you so much for taking the time to play my game and write such detailed feedback! I really appreciate it. There are a lot of good points here that I’ll definitely keep in mind as I continue working on it.

The demo version you played doesn’t include the tutorial that I’ve already implemented at the beginning of the full game, so some of the things you mentioned, especially the controls, the story and the reasons behind what the player is doing, are explained there.

As for the cats, they’re actually my own cats! 😄 I wanted to include them in the game and make them part of the story, so it’s nice that you noticed them.

Thanks again for spending the time on my project and for all the suggestions. Feedback like this is really helpful!
